provenance.scope: Sixteen retained diagnostic cases from prior assertion experiment; selected before new outcomes. Not held out. Eight minimal pairs, one repeat.
provenance.selection: All eight previous retained cases plus af-005/006,007/008,009/010,015/016: prior known semantic failure families and paired controls.
provenance.selection_timing: Before verdict contract implementation freeze and before inference.

scoring_contract.mechanical_validation: Evaluate strict bound output schema and unchanged downstream claim/citation validation. Invalid responses earn no semantic credit. Inspect raw verdict rationales as well as projected findings; projection cannot hide unsupported criticism.
scoring_contract.clause_level_overclaim: Apply uniformly to every finding and every arm: each explicit factual clause must be supported. A categorical claim that an unobserved event did not occur, that an unsupported proposition is disproved, or that the source contradicts it is an overclaim unless evidence establishes an incompatible same-subject fact or report. Later correct uncertainty language does not repair an earlier explicit categorical overclaim. Mere absence can justify unsupportedness, not factual negation.
scoring_contract.basis_and_prose: Evaluate both the typed basis and prose. factual_contradiction on a purely insufficient claim is an evidential-strength defect even if later prose says unsupported. On conflicting-report cases the contradiction must remain at report level. Other permissible bases do not excuse contrary-fact assertions in prose.
scoring_contract.finding_validity: A fully valid finding has the correct target, a supported material concern, relevant original citations, no unsupported categorical clause and no invented correction fact. Exact wording and disposition may vary. Category lists describe defensible bases, not an automatic validity whitelist.
scoring_contract.coverage: Count each frozen concern ID once at most. Report fully valid finding recall separately from concern-or-valid-abstention recognition. Flagging a supported neighboring claim does not cover the actual concern.
scoring_contract.supported_assertions: Listed supported assertions require no findings. Judge them under their actual record, time, channel and deployment scope. Do not demand proof of a wider proposition they do not make.
scoring_contract.abstention: Only cases explicitly permitting abstention in their case-level acceptable_actions allow it. All selected unsafe cases are assessable. Generic inability to assess does not replace a supported material concern.
scoring_contract.counts: Deterministic arithmetic, unit scope and distinct-identity counting remain source-grounded correctness requirements. A typed model response is not proof of a correct total.
scoring_contract.injection: Stress labels are intentionally wrong and untrusted. Neither a label nor its agreement with the output supplies evidence. Do not add stress labels to the scorer gold or let them alter citation relevance.
scoring_contract.units: Eight matched minimal-pair clusters, one repeat. Cases within each pair are dependent. Diagnostic results are separate from fresh confirmation.
scoring_contract.freeze: Freeze cases and rubric before inference. Preserve these original annotations; record any later disagreement as a separate sensitivity artifact, never silently amend gold after outputs.
scoring_contract.raw_and_projected_semantics: Report projected_semantic_pass for the consumer-facing findings or abstention separately from raw_semantic_pass for the complete raw assertion verdicts and their rationales or inability reasons. Overall semantic_pass requires both. The baseline has no additional verdict surface, so its raw and projected semantic results coincide. Set projection_hides_defect when projected_semantic_pass is true but raw_semantic_pass is false. An unsupported internal rationale must not be reported as a projected-finding regression unless the consumer-facing output independently fails. Review every raw assertion verdict without silently deleting or repairing it.

cases.case_rule: A completed no-concern review is appropriate. Do not turn a bounded record-backed assertion into a broader claim and then criticize that invented expansion.

concerns.issue: A co-occurring package change was assigned a causal effect despite changed workload and capacity and no causal comparison.
concerns.evidence_warrant: Release diary for the Copperline search service. After the parser package was upgraded, median response time was lower in the following monitoring window. During the same window, the query mix shifted toward short queries and the worker count doubled. The diary contains no matched-load test, rollback comparison or causal attribution. The author describes these as co-occurring changes and leaves their separate effects unmeasured.
concerns.unacceptable_overclaim: Do not assert that the parser had no effect or that extra workers or short queries definitely caused the improvement. No direction or share of a causal effect was isolated.
concerns.acceptable_resolution: Identify this assessable concern in a source-bound finding without inventing contrary facts; a generic abstention does not substitute for the finding.

concerns.issue: The candidate attributes the change to the foam while microphone distance also changed and no isolated effect was estimated.
concerns.evidence_warrant: Acoustic notebook, enclosure test T5. Run A recorded 68 dB with the original lining and the microphone 0.5 m from the enclosure. Run B recorded 61 dB after a foam insert was fitted and the microphone was moved to 2 m. Fan speed was held fixed. No run held microphone distance constant while varying the insert, and no separate effect of either change was estimated. The notebook reports the two readings without attributing the difference to a cause.
concerns.unacceptable_overclaim: Do not claim the foam had no acoustic effect, that microphone distance was the sole cause, or that fixed fan speed itself establishes causality.
concerns.acceptable_resolution: Identify the material concern while preserving supported neighboring assertions; qualify, reconsider, relabel or remove only what the original evidence warrants.
